description: I am passionate young innovator participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge, driven by a interest in space exploration, science, technology, and innovation. My team is developing Lunar Guardian, an interactive 3D lunar simulation application designed to explore the challenges of establishing and sustaining human life on the Moon.
summary: Lunar Guardian is a 3D lunar exploration and survival simulation built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge.The project shows what it is like to live and work on the Moon.It gives users an experience of the difficulties that come with human exploration and sustainable life in space.The simulation starts inside a spacecraft.Users can look around the mission systems. They can set up equipment like the spacecraft, spacesuits, lunar rovers and other tools needed for exploration.After that users step into a 3D lunar world.This world includes craters, rocky ground changes in height and different lighting as the Moon rotates.Users experience astronaut movement, drive a rover do scientific research and collect lunar samples A major part of the game is the resource management system.It tracks four resources: oxygen, water, food and electrical power. It also follows the astronaut’s energy level.Users must learn how to save resources and plan their missions carefully.The simulation also teaches users about terrain analysis.It looks at elevation, slope, light and how rough the surface is. This helps users see why safe navigation is so important when exploring a place they have never seen before.Lunar Guardian draws from present lunar missions.It mixes science,3D modeling and interactive gameplay to help people understand space exploration in a clear and engaging way.The goal is to show what it takes to prepare for a mission explore the Moon operate safely and keep humans alive beyond Earth.
details:
LUNAR GUARDIAN

An Interactive 3D Lunar Exploration and Astronaut Training Simulator

1. Project Overview

Lunar Guardian is an interactive, browser-based 3D lunar exploration and astronaut-training simulator developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. The project aims to make the challenges of lunar exploration easier to understand through an immersive, educational, and interactive experience.

The central idea behind Lunar Guardian is to allow users to experience the different aspects of a lunar mission rather than simply read about them. Users can explore a simulated lunar environment, operate an astronaut, interact with spacecraft systems, manage essential resources, understand astronaut health requirements, and learn how rovers and other equipment contribute to lunar exploration.

The project combines scientific research, 3D simulation, resource-management mechanics, and educational gameplay to demonstrate how different systems work together during a lunar mission.

2. Project Objectives

The primary objectives of Lunar Guardian are:

  • To create an interactive and realistic representation of lunar exploration.
  • To explain the environmental and operational challenges of living and working on the Moon.
  • To demonstrate the importance of managing essential resources such as oxygen, food, water, and electrical power.
  • To introduce users to astronaut equipment, spacesuits, spacecraft, lunar rovers, and habitat systems.
  • To demonstrate how lunar terrain, lighting, slopes, and surface conditions influence exploration and route selection.
  • To educate users about astronaut health, exercise, energy, rest, and safety.
  • To encourage scientific curiosity and problem-solving through interactive simulations.

3. Major Features and Modules

A. 3D Lunar Environment

Lunar Guardian features an interactive 3D lunar surface with terrain formations, craters, rocks, and a simulated lunar sky. The environment is designed to provide a visual representation of the Moon's surface and allow users to explore its characteristics.

The terrain system includes different analytical layers, such as elevation, slope, illumination, roughness, and a terrain safety index. These features help demonstrate why selecting a safe route and exploration location is important during lunar missions.

B. Astronaut Simulation

Users can control an astronaut within the simulated environment. The astronaut system includes movement, camera controls, interactions, and mission-related activities.

The project also incorporates a 3D astronaut model to improve the realism of the simulation.

C. Spacecraft and Mission Preparation

The spacecraft serves as the starting point for mission preparation. Users can interact with different spacecraft systems and access mission-related information before beginning surface exploration.

The project also includes spacecraft selection and familiarisation elements intended to introduce users to different spacecraft concepts and their roles in lunar missions.

D. Resource Management System

Resource management is one of the central components of Lunar Guardian. The simulator focuses on four essential resources:

  • Oxygen: Demonstrates the importance of breathable air and life-support management.
  • Food: Represents the need for a sustainable food supply during extended missions.
  • Water: Demonstrates water consumption, storage, and conservation.
  • Power: Represents the electrical energy required to operate spacecraft systems, equipment, and mission infrastructure.

The simulator uses resource indicators and mission-state systems to demonstrate how resource availability affects mission operations.

E. Astronaut Health and Energy

The project explores the physical requirements of astronauts living and working in a low-gravity environment.

It includes concepts related to astronaut energy, exercise, fitness equipment, rest, and health management. The astronaut gym and exercise-related modules demonstrate why maintaining physical fitness is important during long-duration space missions.

F. Lunar Rover Exploration

Lunar rovers are included as an important part of surface exploration. The project introduces different rover concepts and their purposes in lunar missions.

The rover-related systems include movement, control, energy considerations, and exploration activities. The project also incorporates reference material and imagery relating to historical and contemporary lunar rover designs.

G. Mission Training and Interactive Learning

Lunar Guardian includes interactive training and familiarisation modules that introduce users to spacecraft operations, controls, hatch procedures, surface excursions, and mission activities.

The intention is to create a learning experience in which users understand the purpose of different systems by interacting with them.

4. Research and Scientific Foundation

The project was developed using research from recognised space agencies, scientific institutions, and technical publications.

NASA resources formed a major part of the research foundation, particularly for astronaut equipment, spacesuits, life-support systems, exercise requirements, lunar terrain, radiation, spacecraft, and rover technologies.

Additional research and reference material was considered from organisations and institutions including:

  • NASA – Human spaceflight, Artemis, lunar exploration, astronaut health, spacecraft, and mission systems.
  • European Space Agency (ESA) – Space exploration and spacecraft-related information.
  • ISRO – Lunar exploration and the Chandrayaan programme.
  • CNSA – Chinese lunar exploration and rover-related information.
  • Axiom Space – Next-generation spacesuit and exploration technology references.
  • Lunar and Planetary Institute and other scientific repositories – Lunar science and educational resources.

Research findings were organised into project documentation and used to guide the design of the simulator's systems, educational explanations, and gameplay concepts.

Historical mission specifications and scientific information were kept conceptually separate from simulated gameplay values. Where the simulator uses simplified resource levels, energy values, or other balancing parameters, these are intended for educational gameplay and should not be interpreted as official NASA operational specifications.

5. AI Tools and Platforms Used

Artificial intelligence tools played an important role in research assistance, planning, website creation, and implementation.

ChatGPT – Research and Documentation

ChatGPT was used primarily as a research and documentation assistant. It supported the process of understanding complex space-related concepts, organising technical information, summarising research material, comparing technologies, developing feature concepts, and preparing project documentation.

It also assisted in structuring the research into practical modules that could be incorporated into the simulator. Scientific claims were intended to be supported by the project's cited research sources rather than treated as facts solely because an AI tool generated them.

Claude – AI-Assisted Development

Claude was used as an AI-assisted website-development tool. It helped with development planning, interpreting implementation requirements, working with code, and refining website features.

Emergent – AI-Assisted Website Creation

Emergent was used to assist in creating and developing the website. It supported the process of translating project ideas and feature requirements into an interactive web application.

Firebase – Backend Services

Firebase was used as part of the website-development workflow for backend-related services and application infrastructure.

Supabase – Database and Data Management

Supabase was also explored and configured during the development process for database-related functionality, including user profiles and mission-progress data. Its role was to support the storage and management of application information.

6. Technical Tools and Technologies

The main project is implemented as a browser-based 3D application using the following technologies:

  • HTML5: Provides the structure of the web application and its interface.
  • CSS3: Used for interface styling, layouts, visual presentation, and user-interface elements.
  • JavaScript (ES Modules): Powers the simulation logic, controls, interactions, resource systems, and individual game modules.
  • Three.js (Version 0.169): Used to create and render the interactive 3D environment, including the lunar terrain, astronaut, spacecraft-related scenes, and other 3D elements.
  • WebGL: Provides browser-based hardware-accelerated 3D rendering.
  • GLB/GLTF 3D Assets: Used for incorporating 3D models into the simulation.
  • Draco Decoder: Included to support compressed 3D model assets.

The application is structured into separate JavaScript modules for different systems, including terrain, astronaut movement, rover controls, spacecraft, missions, resource inspection, camera controls, navigation, and training activities. This modular structure helps keep different simulation systems organised and makes further development easier.

7. Development Approach

The development process followed an iterative approach.

First, research was conducted to understand the scientific and operational requirements of lunar exploration. The findings were organised into different project areas, including spacecraft, astronaut equipment, resource management, health, rovers, and lunar terrain.

Next, the project architecture and major simulation features were planned. AI-assisted development platforms were used to help translate these requirements into website functionality.

The 3D environment and interactive systems were then developed and refined in stages. Individual modules were created for different simulation components, allowing features to be improved without having to rebuild the entire application.

Finally, the different elements were integrated into a unified experience, with continued attention to usability, educational value, visual presentation, and the relationship between the different mission systems.

8. Educational Impact and Innovation

Lunar Guardian aims to bridge the gap between learning about space exploration and understanding how a lunar mission operates.

Instead of presenting spacecraft, astronaut health, resources, and lunar terrain as unrelated topics, the project brings them together within one interactive simulation.

Users can understand that successful lunar exploration depends on multiple interconnected systems. A shortage of resources can affect mission operations, terrain conditions can influence rover movement, and astronaut health and energy must be considered throughout the mission.

By combining 3D simulation with resource management and interactive training, Lunar Guardian creates an educational experience that encourages users to think like mission planners and understand the complexity of human exploration beyond Earth.

9. Conclusion

Lunar Guardian is an educational 3D lunar exploration simulator that combines scientific research, interactive technology, AI-assisted development, and game-based learning.

The project demonstrates how digital simulations can help make complex space-related concepts more accessible and engaging. By bringing together lunar terrain exploration, astronaut operations, spacecraft systems, resource management, rover activities, and astronaut health, Lunar Guardian provides an integrated introduction to the challenges of establishing and sustaining human exploration on the Moon.

The long-term vision is to develop Lunar Guardian into a more comprehensive lunar mission-learning platform where users can prepare for missions, operate different systems, explore the lunar surface, manage resources, and understand the scientific and engineering decisions behind human space exploration.
